REVISING MY OWN PROPOSAL. Evidence from the comparative review of rMVPA (the owner's own package, /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/rMVPA) says a shipped dataset is the wrong fix, or at least not the first one.

rMVPA also has no data/ directory. It solves the same problem with a GENERATOR:

  R/dataset.R:67  gen_sample_dataset(D, nobs, response_type, data_mode, spacing,
                                     blocks, nlevels, external_test, ntest_obs,
                                     split_by, na_cols)

  Constructing_Datasets.Rmd:62  ds <- gen_sample_dataset(D = c(6,6,6), nobs = 80,
                                                         blocks = 4, nlevels = 2)

That one function is why rMVPA reaches a searchlight RSA map in six statements from library() with no files on disk:

  library(rMVPA)
  ds  <- gen_sample_dataset(D = c(8,8,8), nobs = 40, blocks = 4, nlevels = 2)
  model_rdm <- as.matrix(stats::dist(seq_len(40)))
  des <- rsa_design(~ model_rdm, list(model_rdm = model_rdm), block_var = ds$design$block_var)
  mod <- rsa_model(ds$dataset, des, distmethod = 'pearson', regtype = 'pearson')
  res <- run_searchlight(mod, radius = 4, method = 'standard')

A generator beats a shipped dataset on every axis that matters here:

  - no data/ directory, so no lazy-load surface and no CRAN size budget
  - the reader can vary nobs, blocks, and nlevels and watch the answer move, which
    teaches the estimand far better than one frozen matrix
  - it directly reduces the sequencing hazard raised in the body of this bead: no data
    files means the certified tarball does not acquire a data payload while
    bd-01KZXFZ4WRKASSWYMDSECG8FED is still open. It is still new code and still
    enlarges the R CMD check example surface, so the pass-42 ordering point stands,
    but the collision is much smaller than what I first proposed.
  - it is a form the owner already uses and already maintains, so it needs no new
    convention argument

REVISED PROPOSAL: a gen_* generator returning a ready-to-use relation with declared
partition structure, realistic feature count, and a KNOWN generative model, so the
docs can state what the right answer is and show the package recovering it. That last
property is the one rMVPA's generator does NOT have and effectagram should, because
this package's whole claim is about what a cross-generalized estimate means. A
generator with known ground truth lets the introduction end on 'here is the effect we
planted, recovered, and here is why the estimate went slightly negative' instead of on
unlabeled numbers. That single move would convert the negative-estimate policy from a
caveat the reader must accept on faith into something they watch happen.

CAUTION AGAINST MY OWN PROPOSAL: a generator makes it easy to demo the package on data
whose noise structure is nothing like fMRI, which would let the docs look healthy while
saying nothing about real use. The generative model must be declared in the docs, not
buried in the function body.
